paragraphs.text: The people of Amrou were scattered by war and driven into hiding. Scouts maintain the beacon fires that signal "return" and "home."
The paradise of Amrou Haven had become a field of cinders. Its people struggled to survive, hoping to see visions of its past in the strange storms that quickly passed.
"My people swore to protect Benalia to the end. It is battered, but yet stands, as do we."
"Each place we see is as ruined and lifeless as the last. So here we stay, because this ruin is *ours*."
"We have a proud history of self-sacrifice. But it is easy, in these bleak times, to find one among us who is eager to die for any cause." —Tavalus, acolyte of Korlis
"In my dreams, I hear the voices of my future selves who have died in times yet to come. I use that knowledge to avoid those dark futures and continue my search for peace."
"One arrow keenly fired might prevent more battlefield wounds than I could treat."
Bind the mind rather than the wrist, and you stop the intent to harm before it starts.
"Heed my words, traveler. Plagues, war, desolation . . . all mere hints of what is yet to come from Dominaria's vault of horrors."
It disappears each time with the hope that it will not return to the same desolation it left behind.
A focal point for time rifts, Foriys contends simultaneously with foes both new and old.
"Where metal is tainted and wood is scarce, we are best armed by faith." —Tavalus, acolyte of Korlis
A thousand years removed from her home, her news of war had lost its context, but not its relevance.
After Efrava was destroyed, the cat warriors scattered across Dominaria. Those who followed Jedit's example were strong enough to survive the ravages of apocalypse.
Studying the journals of the necromage Nevinyrral leaves disciples gripped with the urge to exercise his draconian judgment.
"I have been brought to this place and I cannot leave. I may be free of the amber, but I am still in prison."
It was a moment in time, cast in stone—a moment whose time had come again.
It is best to conquer dragons before they hatch. —Femeref adage
Like a great bellows it hisses, and its kin, both living and dead, are lifted to safety.
"They have long kept us under attack, but we do not lack for ammunition. The very bodies of our foes arm us against them." —Adom Capashen, Benalish hero
Some timelines forever fray, branch, and intermingle. Others end abruptly.
"Those who endure in the face of suffering, those whose faith shines long in evil days, they shall see salvation." —*Song of All*, canto 904
"They encircled our patrol with the stealth of snakes, corralling us like livestock." —Merrik Aidar, Benalish patrol
His blade came down upon the neck of a goblin—but not the one he had charged. When Tivadar looked up, the world he had known was gone.
"I have spied them, wandering and watching—but for what? I fear they watch for us." —Yonat of Amrou
"Teferi snapped his fingers, and the viashino started clucking like a chicken. Silly, yes, but exactly the thing we needed to break the stifling tension." —Jhoira, master artificer
Water calls to water, and the world is left exhausted and withered in its wake.
Fendros gasped as he watched the spell drip from the ends of his fingers. He moved his foot, afraid to disturb the spot where it lay slain.
"Sages who take the time to verify their sources are rewarded for their diligence." —Jhoira, to Teferi
They wait in darkened depths, laughing eagerly.
The rift remained open for days, sluicing ancient seawater. It closed only after the last great tentacle squirmed its way through.
What happens when it is the dream that wakes and the sleeper that fades into memory?
They study the deeds of their traitorous ancestors, hoping the stories may reveal a way back to the physical world.
Unable to touch items of value, he goes forth to steal secrets instead.
Once a vision of constancy in the sky, the moon had long been hidden from view by the haze that chokes the heavens. The very sight of it had become a sign that change was in the air.
"Keep your pace steady through the haze, lest you step on the heels of your future self or trip the self a moment behind you." —Teferi
They evolved the ability to concentrate their neural activity into a single pulse, causing a disruptive but usually suicidal blast of psionic energy.
Clairvoyants across Dominaria were driven mad by the overload from the widening time rifts, while other random folk gained the gift of future sight.
"What wears down my people most, I think, is not the danger, but the endless screeching outside our camp." —Merrik Aidar, Benalish patrol
These slivers, trapped between worlds since the Rathi overlay, are among the last to claim direct lineage from the lost Sliver Queen.
"If it returns years hence, our knowledge of how to combat it will be that much greater." —Andorel, Tolarian sentinel
The brutish mage's version of thinking.
Drakelings fish with their tails, angling to snare succulent thoughts and memories on their psychic hooks.
"By thorn and by stone, we will fight to see the day when beauty returns to this world."
As fickle as lightning, as slippery as an eel.
To save this plane, he must forsake all others.
"Slivers are guided only by simple instinct. Advance the hive, and you will be welcomed. Impede the hive, and you will face unrelenting opposition." —Freyalise
As the temporal fractures spread and time itself slowly fell apart, visitors started to appear from across the past and future, and those native to the present began to disappear.
"Great books are meant to be read, then read again backwards or upside down!" —Ettovard, Tolarian archivist
"It is not just our people I try to rescue. It is our culture, and our hope that we can return to greatness."
An eyeblink later, all that remained of the tree-beast was the breeze of its momentum.
The rulers of old Dominaria kept assassins on retainer. However, the true loyalty of these master killers was always to their peers. This elite brotherhood survived the fall of the old royal order.
"Fascinating . . . These creatures display the paradox of tenacity and purposed self-destruction I have sought to breed into my thrulls." —Endrek Sahr, master breeder
The ritual was normally performed only by horrors and pit spawn. Lesser mages had but one sanity to crack in the casting.
A tomb-eye may remain shut for centuries. It opens when it sees a world as twisted and hollow as the wretch beneath its lid.
Those who forget the horrors of the past are doomed to re-meet them.
"The surface of the land is blanched with salt, but the soil beneath is reddened with death—a fertile ground for necromancy." —Lim-Dûl the Necromancer
"Edahlis, what *is* that thing? We should have stayed in Yavimaya . . . ." —Aznaph, greenseeker
Just a small touch of magic can harness the debilitating power of Urborg's poisonous winds.
The hymn's melody has persisted since Tourach's time, but the words changed to invoke the phobias of each listener.
"Behold! The image of the enemy and all that she has. Trust your envy, and take it."
They traverse the mana-starved wastes in search of richer lands.
Though Dominaria's queenless slivers lack a single purpose, in some the instinct for self-sacrifice remains extremely strong.
"The undead are not 'awakened.' They are evicted when there is no room left in the pit for more bodies."
A sliver shares everything with its hive—even its afflictions.
"This soil knows well the taste of the dead. Give it the hunger for a living meal, and it can become a deadly ally." —Ezrith, druid of the Dark Hours
The living is all it eats.
Most living things were weakened and stunted in the ruinous aftermath of the Phyrexian invasion, but a few grew more horrid than ever.
"Great losses often bring only a numb shock. To truly plunge a victim into misery, you must overwhelm him with many small sufferings." —Ratadrabik of Urborg
"What good is your blade without your breath?" —Greht, Gathan warlord
Some mages tapped into the time rifts, forcing upon others alternate timelines in which unimaginable horrors befall them.
"Even swamps need sustenance. We will give it to them, and in turn, they will sustain us." —Ezrith, druid of the Dark Hours
At the epicenter of the Rathi overlay, the City of Traitors did not align with Dominaria. Many of its inhabitants were caught between the two worlds.
"I have become a gourmet of sorts. Each soul has its own distinctive flavor. The art is in inviting the right company to the feast."
They draw upon the strength of their hive and of their victims.
"Lemurs? Is that all? Finally, something harmless . . ." —Norin the Wary
The time rifts remind Yavimaya of the enemies of its past and provide fresh fuel for its fires.
Fervid shamans willingly submit to shockers in hopes of glimpsing the fortunes of the future.
"This can't be Jamuraa. We could not have failed her this badly . . . ."
In the erupting heart of Bogardan, it's hard to tell hurtling volcanic rocks from pouncing volcanic beasts.

As the time streams grew more and more unstable, Dominaria's creatures struggled to adapt. The intense pressures led to many dead ends but also to lethal new forms that appeared as suddenly as the ashen rains.
"The day is mine! I sent three such creatures against my foe, then watched as my magefire popped her soldiers like overripe spleenfruits." —Dobruk the Unstable, pyromancer
"They'd pour out of the warrens to make war (and to make room for the littering matrons)." —*Sarpadian Empires, vol. IV*
To a fire elemental, fools and fuels are one and the same.
With the evincars gone, flowstone became erratic and wild, a source of power for mages more desperate than wise.

"A rift opened, and our arrows were abruptly stilled. To move was to push the world. But the sliver's claw still twitched, red wounds appeared in Thed's chest, and ribbons of blood hung in the air." —Adom Capashen, Benalish hero
He takes out his fear of heights on anything above his head.
Mages often seek to emulate the powerful relics lost to time and apocalypse.
Some time rifts didn't take away the people but just the ground they stood on.
"Everybody but me—CHARGE!"
They warn the army of danger as they squawk past in swift retreat.
"A gargoyle's meat can be carved with an ordinary cleaver, but for its petrous hide . . ." —Asmoranomardicadaistinaculdacar, *The Underworld Cookbook*
"I have a bad feeling about this."
"Crispy! Scarback! Load another volcano-ball." —Stumphobbler Thuj, Orcish captain
"Echoes of the Mirari's power yet linger." —Zyd, Kamahlite druid
Their flesh is as sodden as the fens in which they live, oozing to fill any wound and squishing to absorb any blow.
Arc mages aren't known for their patience.
The Keldons used the toxic vents in the cracked earth to bolster their home's defenses.
The barbarians of Pardia are long dead, but its mountains still smolder with rage.
The shaman of the tribe is responsible for keeping track of all its treasures, including angry pets and cursed lamps of fiery doom.
"That which would be a fatal mutation in any other species is merely a source of new powers. I am intrigued, yet too fearful to examine it more closely." —Rukarumel, field journal
Radha was born in Skyshroud, but her temper is undeniably Keldon.
"Find your courage in a desperate moment, and you turn the tide of history. So sayeth the bey."
With a great roar, the land opened like a titan's yawn, with teeth of blackened rock and a lolling tongue of magma.
"Obey!"
The bears wade into time rifts to feed. They do not fear the storms, and they are quick enough to snatch prey just as it blinks in or out of time.
"Sometimes the best plan is neither fighting nor running." —Freyalise
These days, trackers must follow their quarry over years as well as miles.
"When a sliver of this breed enters the hive, the others claw each other in frenzied fits, thereby ensuring their rapid growth." —Rukarumel, field journal
"The land is weary. Even Skyshroud is depleted. We must find another source of mana—one that is growing despite our withering world." —Freyalise
Its venom induces a fever that causes its victims to relive the attack in recurring, haunting visions.
"A rumor passes among the snakes, whispered by the rushes, inspiring the seekers: the goddess Freyalise is alive in Skyshroud."
Time rifts bring tunneling beasts of old into the hard, dry earth of the present. Most die there, trapped, but the mightiest burst through the surface.
Long ago, the solitary gnarr was a sign of good luck. Now they have become wild pack hunters, a sign of impending danger.
"Give up these unnatural weapons, these scrolls. Heart and mind and fist are enough." —Zyd, Kamahlite druid
"What would Urza think, I wonder, if he could hear how the nature mages still snarl at his name, but venerate the work of his apprentice?" —Teferi, to Jhoira
Sometimes even humble forest creatures were gifted with mighty emanations from the past.

"The colossal thing rumbled over the ridge, tree husks crumbling before it. The ones we were already fighting howled as it came, their muscles suddenly surging, and we knew it was time to flee." —Llanach, Skyshroud ranger
"The forests have succumbed to ruin, but the spirit of Krosa remains alive and vital in these devouring spores." —Zyd, Kamahlite druid
"Life gives way to death, and death to new life. Nature feeds upon her own decay." —Ezrith, druid of the Dark Hours
The elder who carries the ancestral mantle of Jacques le Vert is tasked with his ancient mission: to protect the creatures of Pendelhaven.
When it snared a passing cockatrice, its own soul darkly doubled.
It died with the forest, yet both linger on in twisted form.
Their calls unheeded by the withered forests, nature shamans channeled the life force of their brethren.
To treefolk's sense of time, ages pass as hours. They stood as witnesses to the apocalypse, the years of which they saw as one cacophonous, ultra-destructive moment.
"The spirits of old have not left us unguarded." —Uros, Pendelhaven elder
Each new generation of slivers evolves to assimilate the strengths of the prey upon which their progenitors fed.
Centuries of temporal strife had stripped Dominaria of its natural defenses, but nature fought back with armies constructed of little more than grime and sunlight.
The constant shifting of Dominaria's shredded timeline played havoc with its atmosphere, combining savage electrical storms from ages past.
"Might of ancient wood and stone, Into spirit, flesh, and bone."
"The hermit dies. The outcast dies. The lone wolf dies. Only those who stick together survive this world." —Uros, Pendelhaven elder
"The sight of my thallids still thriving is a bittersweet welcome to this cold waste."
Ground into the footprints of the ravaging herd were clumps of salt from Benalia, moss from Llanowar, dust from Hurloon, and ash from as far as Urborg.
With no jungle left to contain it, the "plague of daggers" spread across Dominaria.
The parched earth still shielded those few souls with the heart to call it home.
"They are here, and they are hungry. And what they do not eat, they burn. Yavimaya is lost. We must leave now for Skyshroud." —Edahlis, greenseeker
"This breed is on the cusp of evolution. It burns away the markings that connect it to a queen that no longer heeds its call. It seeks a new master. Perhaps I can give it one." —Freyalise
"Since the last sliver arrived, even our mightiest relics splinter into shards as soon as we bring them against the hive." —Llanach, Skyshroud ranger
"Rats and jackals feast in his swath, but even they will not walk with him." —Mangara
A sojourn through time gave dark inspiration to one gifted young mind.
"When struck, its hide shimmers through sequences of color—a signaling language I am eager to unravel." —Rukarumel, field journal
In the blink of an eye, she strode from deep snow to dusty waste. From the crease of light behind her, a voice rang hollow: "Saffi, wait for me . . . ."
"I am the blood of the ur-dragon, coursing through all dragonkind."
Moments after a fickle rift dropped Stonebrow in the waste of his beloved Krosa, he took up his axe in rage-blind vengeance.
With their factories long destroyed, some of Mishra's creations still toil in remote areas, endlessly performing and reperforming their last orders.
Its buzzing is the sound of its inner mechanisms, ever winding down.
"A tome stored in its light is as crisp as the day it was written." —Ettovard, Tolarian archivist
"This item is not from . . . now. It reflects a sky no longer ours and gleams with hope that does not exist." —Tavalus, acolyte of Korlis
Rath's evincars used hivestones to control the slivers, but the overlay put their power into unwitting hands. Now the stones make not masters, but slaves.
Every hour, at the turning of the glass, its owner had whispered to the locket, seeding it with secrets. This would be her legacy, her memory, if the rifts should take her.
A last wisp of paradise in a fallen world.
It bends not light but mana, aligning its chaotic currents into the sharp angles necessary for the mystic's purposes.
The past still lives within its pages, waiting for its time to come again.

Venser admired his handiwork and smiled. His first prototype had joined with the hive mind all too well, running with the brood and becoming a predator itself. This one, he thought, would be accepted into the hive but still obey his commands.
Its secrets once wrought the greatest artifice ever known. Now crabs loot the rubble to decorate their shells.
Dust-spiked winds eroded the stones, but the ground where they had stood still holds power.
"They're still here?! The cockroach may have finally met its match." —Teferi
Where scavengers nest in hollowed-out rib cages and chittering crawlers peer from empty eye sockets, few dare to trespass.
Take two steps north into the unsettled future, south into the unquiet past, east into the present day, or west into the great unknown.
"Though their ideals are leagues apart, Urza's and Mishra's creations have a surprising harmony with one another." —Tocasia, journal entry
It is everywhere you've ever been.
